items.topic: Coding agents raise the bar for software engineering discipline
items.text:
The more time I spend working with coding agents, the more convinced I am that they make software engineering even harder

We can do amazing things with them, but unlocking their full potential requires extraordinary discipline and knowledge

quote_tweet.text:
Bury your head in the ground at your own risk. I aim to not jump on any hype trains, but since Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2 + the harnesses it was clear that these things can write code nearly as good as I can in my best language; better in other languages.

But we won't see non-devs push production code for a long time; possibly forever, if you ask me. Software still needs to be built in robust ways, and it's our profession to do this well, and use the new tools we have, which create new and interesting (+tough!) challenges

items.topic: Compressing tool-call details in agent transcripts
items.text: I guess the real question here is: do you actually still care about the tool calls in the transcript? If they are getting worse and worse, maybe they should be compressed? I wonder what people expect at this point.

quote_tweet.text: Mario proposes to 'write an extension that inserts "mofo, don't use bash to edit files"'. Because this is my current experience with Opus 5.5 :(

items.topic: Reviewing model file edits through git diffs
items.text: Not sure what the path should be to making the experience of all those models using code to edit files acceptable.  The claude hack of adding everything to git and then diffing it is definitely an option but very heavy handed :-/
github, love ya, but why did you change the default sorting of issues from "last created" to "best match"? best matching what exactly? in what world is that sensible? :/

items.topic: Reviewing agent edits through diffs instead of tool calls
items.text:
i akso said "don't fight the model, give in to its RL, let if flow over you"

i personally haven't given a fart about edit tool calls in a long while. i just look at diffs in VS Code, either while the agent is working, or after. which also gives me code nav and other things.

items.topic: Reviewing agent changes in VS Code
items.text:
something @giuseppegurgone taught me at the first claude code anonymous, many hundred years ago.

i don't use my bespoke review tool anymore. i inspect stuff in VS Code, with code nav/debugging/whatever i need to grok the code, then leave BOZOs for the agent.

items.topic: Auditing AI-generated tests for low-value coverage
items.text: OpenClaw deleted around 400k LOC of its own tests without much change in code coverage. Modern models just love writing tests for every tiny change, even if they aren't useful. This skill helped.

items.topic: Agent workflows should not optimize for transcript waiting
items.text:
My maybe controversial opinion:

If TTFT is important to you, you're doing something wrong.

Don't wait for the agents, make them wait for you.

Don't stare at a single transcript. Do something else.

(Yes, there's a tiny number of exceptions to this.)

quote_tweet.text: playtesting every harness again, i cannot believe how you folks don't lose it over the TUI taking over 50ms to start, and TTFT >2s - these companies are achieving AGI and here we're stuck with the slowpoke harnesses wtf

items.topic: Claude Code plan mode becoming a built-in mod
items.text:
lots feedback here, many of you are planning yourself & don't need plan mode

others prefer the UX of entering a mode where Claude is just thinking & brainstorming with you

my plan is to:
- make plan mode into a built-in mod
- allow mods to add new modes or override shift+tab

quote_tweet.text:
we’re thinking of killing plan mode and using the shift+tab hotkey to adjust effort levels

I don’t think the models need plan mode anymore, but if you’re a plan mode diehard would love to get your feedback on why

items.text: my rule for sharing Claude output (PRs, artifacts, messages) is that I only do it if I would be happy sharing the prompts
